name: Glenary's
why_it_matters: British Raj-era confectionery opened 1885 by an Italian family (Vado, later Glenary's); among the oldest eateries in any Indian hill station. Three floors today — bakery counter on ground, café on first, Buzz pub on top. Around 170 staff with no formal retirement policy.
insider_tip: The bakery counter on the ground floor opens by 7am — the cinnamon rolls are baked twice daily and gone by 11. Skip the café upstairs at peak season; takeaway and walk to Chowrasta Mall is faster.

name: Keventer's
why_it_matters: Founded 1911 by Swedish-Danish dairy entrepreneur Edward Keventer to feed British officers escaping the plains; sold to the Jha family in 1970. The two-storey building sits at the Nehru Road–Chowrasta junction; pork sausages and salami are still locally cured on premises.
insider_tip: Take the staircase to the upper terrace — the open-air seats face Kanchenjunga on a clear morning. Get there by 7:30am for both the view and a table; by 9am the queue runs down to Mall Road.
signature_address: Shop 1, Club Side, Nehru Road, Chowrasta Mall, Darjeeling 734101

name: Sonam's Kitchen
why_it_matters: Tiny eight-seat breakfast room run by Sonam — one of the only places in Darjeeling brewing coffee from freshly roasted beans rather than instant powder. Western breakfast staples (eggs, hash browns, French toast) at locals' prices.
insider_tip: Open from 8am-3pm only; closes between meals on slow days. Coffee orders take 10-12 minutes — Sonam grinds and brews each one.

name: Hot Stimulating Cafe
why_it_matters: Run by Lily (the cook) and her husband Mr K. Rumba on Jawahar Road, en route to the Zoo and Himalayan Mountaineering Institute. Six tables. Cult following for the vegetarian momos and the deadpan signage that names the place.
insider_tip: It's a literal up-the-stairs cafe — easy to miss; look for hand-painted boards above the road. Order momos and thukpa together; portions are small.
signature_address: Lebong Cart Road, near Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, Richmond Hill, Darjeeling 734101

name: Joey's Pub
why_it_matters: Opened 1991 by Puran Gangoba (Uncle Joey) in a bungalow off Laden La Road; closed after his death in 2016 and reopened 2021 in a new building on the same site. Long the British-style pub of choice for Darjeeling's locals — Sikkimese officers, school teachers, regulars from Singamari.
insider_tip: Cash and small notes only — UPI is patchy. Sundays are local-regulars day; arrive before 6pm if you want a window seat.
signature_address: Dr SM Das Road, opposite Big Bazaar, Limbugaon, Darjeeling 734101

name: Hasty Tasty
why_it_matters: Pure-vegetarian Darjeeling fixture for over 18 years — South Indian, North Indian, Punjabi, Gujarati and Jain food on one menu. The default lunch stop for Marwari and Gujarati travellers and the hill town's vegetarian-only diners.
insider_tip: The South Indian thali is the dependable order; the dosas are made on a hotel-grade tawa and travel limp. Open 8:30am-8:30pm; closes early on rainy days.
signature_address: Nehru Road, near Mall Chowrasta, Chauk Bazaar, Darjeeling 734101

name: Penang Restaurant
why_it_matters: Operating since 1972 off Laden La Road opposite Rink Mall; one of the oldest sit-down restaurants in town for Nepali, Tibetan and Chinese cuisine on a single menu. Renovated interiors in 2016 but the kitchen and Gorkha thali remain unchanged.
insider_tip: Approach lane is unmarked and unimpressive — walk through what looks like a service alley off Laden La. Ask for the Gorkha thali by name; the regular menu doesn't list it prominently.
signature_address: 22, Chauk Bazaar, Laden La Road, Rose Bank, Darjeeling 734101
